Signed numbers have both magnitude and direction. The following examples distinguish the operation being taught from nearby but different skills; learners should explain sign decisions in words or on a number line when appropriate.

Publisher student tasks reviewed: Sorting directed number-line arrows; calculating temperatures after signed changes. Original first-party interpretation must preserve the signed quantities and learner-reasoned table/number-line/partner explanation; do not equate an auto-scored number with source activity completion. Student page: https://im.kendallhunt.com/MS/students/2/5/2/index.html.

KeyConcepts.Title: Mathematical meaning
KeyConcepts.Definition: Positive changes point toward larger values.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Positive changes point toward larger values.

KeyConcepts.Title: Operation or model
KeyConcepts.Definition: Negative changes point toward smaller values.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Negative changes point toward smaller values.

KeyConcepts.Title: Verification
KeyConcepts.Definition: Place the next change arrow at the current result.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Place the next change arrow at the current result.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source-goal task 1
WorkedExamples.Question: −3°C warms 7°C: result?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use rational-number arithmetic and check signs and units.
WorkedExamples.Check: Recompute with inverse operations or verify in the stated context.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source-goal task 2

WorkedExamples.Method: Use rational-number arithmetic and check signs and units.
WorkedExamples.Check: Recompute with inverse operations or verify in the stated context.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source-goal task 3

WorkedExamples.Method: Use rational-number arithmetic and check signs and units.
WorkedExamples.Check: Recompute with inverse operations or verify in the stated context.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source-student task — Changing Temperatures
WorkedExamples.Question: A thermometer begins at −6°C, warms by 9°C then cools by 4°C. Draw two directed arrows, and state the final temperature.
WorkedExamples.Method: Build and label a first-party signed-number diagram or table; explain sign conventions, equations and units. Teacher review is required for representation and contextual reasoning.
Steps: Begin at −6 on a signed axis.
Check expression −6+9−4=−1 and label the arrows.
WorkedExamples.Check: Teacher checks direction, tick spacing, arrow sequence and final value.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treating a cooling change as addition of a positive number.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the sign rule, the reference amount or the modeled direction.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use a signed number line, equivalent equation or independent arithmetic check.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Dropping a negative sign while simplifying a rational expression
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: A sign error reverses the mathematical meaning of a change.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Carry signed parentheses and test with an inverse operation.

SummaryPoints: Positive changes point toward larger values.
Negative changes point toward smaller values.
Place the next change arrow at the current result.
